akhfash:7-7.t: He said ﴿خُشَّعاً﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they come out of the graves humbled. Some read ﴿خاشِعا﴾ because it is an attribute placed first, so he treated it like the verb; its counterpart is ﴿خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ﴾.

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ﴾, and ﴿يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ﴾ as an attribute.

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿أَبَشَراً مِّنَّا وَاحِداً نَّتَّبِعُهُ﴾: He put "a human" in the accusative since the interrogative particle fell on it, and He made the verb fall on something connected with it.

akhfash:44-44.t: And He said ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ﴾ ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ﴾: He gave the group a single back in the wording. And He said ﴿وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ﴾, and He said ﴿لاَ يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ﴾.

akhfash:48-49.t:
And He said ﴿ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾ ﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾: He made the touch something tasted, by the latitude of speech; it is said: "How did you find the taste of the beating?" This is figurative (majāz). As for the accusative of ﴿كلّ﴾, it is in the dialect of those who say "عبدَ اللهِ ضَرَبْتُه" (ʿAbd Allāh, I struck him), and that is frequent in the speech of the Arabs. "كلُّ" has also been put in the nominative, in the dialect of those who use the nominative, and in another way as well.
He said ﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ﴾ and made ﴿خَلَقْنَاهُ﴾ an attribute of "thing".

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ﴾: He made the khabar (predicate) singular, for "all".
